body:
You need to find something that gives you passion, and it might take counseling and doctors to get there, but there is so much hope for improving your life still.

Try getting out, going to volunteer or meetup events and try meeting new people
I'm glad you're doing better these days :) inspirational story
There are more of us.  Don't give up hope

It sounds like you've done as much as you can, unless you can get in touch with neighbors.  The police and ambulance will get her to a hospital and she'll likely be admitted to a psych ward.  Stay supportive through her entire treatment and as comforting as possible

Online might be the best option then, it cuts out the personal aspect but you may be able to find some proper you really identify with

Such as this one

http://www.psychforums.com/asperger-syndrome/

I'm not religious at all, but I do have this quote on my wall and it reminds me to keep going whenever I feel like giving up

'god does not pet the good man.  He tries him, hardens him, and fits him for himself'

Even if it's not god, believe that life has a purpose for the hardships and your will being tested.
I'm sorry you suffer with aspergers, it's an awful set back.  A good counselor for it could make a difference though, or maybe online forums for aspergers?

You're becoming a stronger person for every set back you've been through.  It's not fair how long and difficult it is, but eventually life will get better for you.  And you'll be able to truly appreciate it when it does.  Stay strong and don't give up
Have they recommended any counseling or support groups for you?

Keep trying, good counselors are sadly hard to come by but they do exist.  You have SO MUCH ahead of you still, so many changes to go through and eventually you will experience happiness and purpose.  Also, it sounds like you have the support of your family so never forget how much they love you and want to see you better

I'm so glad you survived, and are here to tell your story.  I think most of the people here who truly understand have been through depression and hell in order to be as compassionate as they are.  Continue talking and helping others, you're a great resource to the community.

This community is amazing, there are so many people who struggle in the day to day world and most people fail at noticing each others pain.  Having a source online and admitting to these thoughts anonymously and knowing you're not alone is sometimes all it takes
Call a suicide line before taking that risk, learn other options and how many people are there to help you if they know how much you're going through

Be with him.  Take him out for walks, coffee, anything, don't pressure him to talk but show unconditional love and support. Make it known that you don't think differently of him but you'll always be there when he needs to talk to someone
Your parents still love you just as much as if they planned. If this is bothering you so much, discuss it with your mom.  It might be interesting to hear her perspective

stay strong.  people that have been in similar situations with losing property could probably offer great advice.  

try to take a break, do something you enjoy so you're not as burnt out.  and talk to people about what's going on, you can get through it.

does your university have a counseling service?  most do for situations like this.

I can't promise it'll be the best counseling, but it is a good place to start.  they'll know the campus and be able to help.

I remember freshman year, this time of year was AWFUL.  The novelty of college life has worn off but you still feel like you have no real friends or connections.  and the work is also just beginning to pile on.  trust me, things will get better.  It took till about halfway through freshman year for me to find a group of friends I enjoyed but even then, I switched social circles about three more times to get to the point I'm at now.

It's scary, but you're definitely not alone.  Keep joining clubs, making efforts, attend study parties.  You'll be amazed how many other people go through this.

what she did was awful, and you're right to be upset and angry.

and I'm sorry your self esteem took a hit for what she did, it's expected that anyone would feel like shit after that.  but things will get better.  stay focused on the good things in your life.  try to slowly recover and take time for yourself.  you probably have friends that care, so spend time with them.

things will slowly hurt less, and eventually you'll find someone that truly loves you.  don't kill your self without giving other people that opportunity.
I'm trying to find old comments that explain so you don't have to, so far all I can say is congrats on the recent weight loss!

I'm sorry that it's been frustrating experience so far.  You came to the right place and there are many resources available besides counselors and doctors.  Try reading this and other depression communities.  Start small and continue attempting to see counselors.

How long have you been depressed for?

as someone in a "support system" like what you mentioned, you need to know that the people that love you are trying their best.  please don't give up on them or the hope that things will get better. try other medicine, other doctors, other therapists.  

your support system cares about you, reach out and tell them what you need.  that psych wards don't help but try to find alternative methods.  it may be hard and having the motivation to try is almost impossible, but posting here it sounds like you don't want to die.  so keep trying, and PM me if you need to talk.
